memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.' 'I cannot do it,' Joseph replied to Pharaoh, 'but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires.'" - Gen 41:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is Joseph's great moment. Standing before Pharaoh, with his freedom and future hanging in the balance, he has every reason to impress the king, to talk up his own abilities, to seize the credit. Pharaoh even hands him the opening: "I have heard that you can interpret dreams." But Joseph will not take the glory. "I cannot do it," he says plainly, "but God will give Pharaoh the answer."

What courage and humility this took. Joseph pointed away from himself and straight to God, before the most powerful man on earth, at the very moment his fate depended on Pharaoh's favour. He would rather honour God than promote himself, even when self-promotion might have served him well.

Here is a beautiful pattern for us. When we are gifted, praised, or given a chance to shine, the temptation is to grab the credit and build our own reputation. Joseph shows the better way: to deflect the glory to God and to be a humble witness to Him. His words were not false modesty; they were true worship — giving God the honour that belonged to Him.

May God give us the same courage to point to Him rather than ourselves, especially in the moments when it would be easy and advantageous to take the credit. Whatever gifts or successes come our way, let our lives say, "Not I, but God."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When praised, do I grab the credit or point to God?
2. Do I have the courage to honour God even when self-promotion would help me?
3. How can my life say, "Not I, but God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the humility and courage to point to You rather than myself, even when taking the credit would serve me. Let my life say, "Not I, but God." May all the glory be Yours. Amen.
